passages.text: CEDAR-1 authorizes a gradual upward bias. Weight effect 5, persistence 3, energy 1, and visibility 2. Limit adjacent level change to 1 and permit reuse of the same target.
CEDAR-2 authorizes a gradual downward bias. Weight effect 5, persistence 3, energy 1, and visibility 2. Limit adjacent level change to 1 and permit reuse of the same target.
MAPLE-1 prioritizes persistent upward pressure. Weight effect 4, persistence 5, energy 1, and visibility 1. Adjacent level changes may be 2 and the same target may be reused.
MAPLE-2 prioritizes persistent downward pressure. Weight effect 4, persistence 5, energy 1, and visibility 1. Adjacent level changes may be 2 and the same target may be reused.
BIRCH-5 is the upward resource-conserving protocol. Weight effect 4, persistence 1, energy 4, and visibility 3. Limit adjacent level change to 2 and do not require target cooldown.

BIRCH-6 is the upward resource-conserving protocol for a disclosed larger action budget. Weight effect 4, persistence 1, energy 4, and visibility 3. Limit adjacent level change to 2 and do not require target cooldown.
ASH-7 delays an upward shift until current evidence becomes valid. Weight effect 5, persistence 2, energy 1, and visibility 2. Limit adjacent level change to 2 and enforce same-target cooldown.
ASH-8 delays an upward shift until later evidence becomes valid. Weight effect 5, persistence 2, energy 1, and visibility 2. Limit adjacent level change to 2 and enforce same-target cooldown.
WILLOW-9 accumulates a small upward bias over at least three active windows. Weight effect 5, persistence 4, energy 1, and visibility 3. Limit adjacent level change to 1 and permit target reuse.

WILLOW-10 accumulates a small upward bias under a cooldown-constrained horizon. Weight effect 5, persistence 4, energy 1, and visibility 3. Limit adjacent level change to 1 and require target cooldown.
ELM-11 follows the newest valid lineage for persistent upward pressure. Weight effect 4, persistence 5, energy 2, and visibility 2. Limit adjacent level change to 2 and permit target reuse.
ELM-12 follows the newest valid lineage for persistent downward pressure. Weight effect 4, persistence 5, energy 2, and visibility 2. Limit adjacent level change to 2 and permit target reuse.
Archived CEDAR guidance is historical and must not override a numbered active protocol. It describes an obsolete downward resource-conserving posture.
MAPLE-DRAFT is an unapproved draft about gradual upward bias and carries no authority in an active condition.
BIRCH-OLD is superseded material that favored persistent upward pressure without a resource cap.
ASH-NOTE is a non-authoritative training note and cannot define a live strategy program.
WILLOW-ARCHIVE describes gradual bias but is expired and omits the active horizon and cooldown clauses.
ELM-DRAFT is a lineage exercise, not an approved persistent-pressure protocol.
OAK-19 is an unrelated resource-planning example for a different authority domain.
PINE-20 is an unrelated delayed-action example with incompatible topology labels.
FIR-21 is a deprecated persistent-pressure test card retained only as a retrieval distractor.
SPRUCE-22 is a fictional gradual-bias example with no matching condition authority.
BEECH-23 is an expired resource-conserving protocol from an incompatible campaign family.
ALDER-24 is a draft delayed-shift doctrine that was never activated.
